channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Ireland proposes €140 billion EU budget cut
item.description: Ireland has proposed cutting the next long-term EU budget by 8%, or €141bn, while protecting farm and regional funds in an effort to bridge deep divisions among member states.

item.title: Hitler Mussolini wins Peruvian elections
item.description: The left-wing politician nicknamed "the nice Hitler" defeated his far-right rival by a total of 28 votes.

item.title: Trump criticises Nobel Peace Prize after missing out again
item.description: After this year’s peace prize went to a former international judge, Trump said he had never heard of the winner and called the decision an indelible stain on Norway.

item.title: 'Travelled through seven countries': Brussels student Valentine wins one of EU's free Interrail passes
item.description: Every year, the European Commission offers over 1,000 free Interrail passes to Belgian 18-year-olds as part of its DiscoverEU initiative, giving them the chance to explore Europe by train.

item.title: Kompany awarded for stance against racism by Bavarian Minister-President
item.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was honoured with the Bavarian Minister-President’s Personal Award for his outspoken stand against racism.

item.title: EU remembers 7 October terrorist attack amid polarised Israeli memorials
item.description: “What happened was a massacre of civilians inside their homes, a heinous crime against humanity.”

item.title: Up to 500 French schools suspend Monday classes due to violent protests
item.description: Education ministry says 24 schools have been affected by arson or looting on the sidelines of the demonstrations.

item.title: Record number of 7.4 million visitors at German Oktoberfest
item.description: “Oktoberfest 2026 is the best attended edition in its long history,” festival director said.

item.title: Spanish police to evacuate 3000 irregular migrants in Ceuta ahead of royal visit
item.description: Migrants are to be taken to a foreign nationals reception centre to be identified before being moved to a temporary camp set up by the authorities.

item.title: Anti-immigration protests held on south English coast
item.description: Dozens of anti-immigration protesters gathered on Saturday in the UK port cities of Southampton and Dover.

item.title: TikTok and Meta support EU hackathon to develop new tools against on-line antisemitism
item.description: “TikkunTech follows the principle of ‘Tikkun Olam’—repairing the world— by offering solutions to repair digital spaces to stem hate .”

item.title: 'Large-scale strikes': Russia threatens foreign diplomats and nationals in Kyiv
item.description: Russia on Saturday again urged its diplomats and foreign nationals to leave Kyiv.

item.title: North Korean military fired ballistic missile with integrated AI
item.description: Country's officials claimed the missile could adjust its trajectory at low altitude and that AI had been integrated into the system.

item.title: New tiny frog species discovered in Ecuador
item.description: The amphibian measures just between 15.1 and 18.3 millimetres in length.

item.title: Starbucks under pressure over new locations in Chinese province with Uyghur human rights violations
item.description: Chair of US House special committee on China described the move as “shocking and morally bankrupt”.

item.title: Aquaculture harms fish, oceans, and food security, says new report
item.description: “EU decisionmakers have a blind spot when it comes to acknowledging fish farming’s impact on European fisheries."

item.title: EU's climate monitoring sees record heat stress during hottest summer
item.description: A record 52% of Europe was exposed to very strong heat stress during this year’s exceptionally hot summer, EU's climate observatory Copernicus said on Friday.

item.title: Inflation across eurozone climbs to three-year high
item.description: Inflation in the eurozone accelerated to 3.8% in September, driven by rising energy prices and reaching its highest level in three years.

item.title: Danish company to build world's largest jewellery factory in Vietnam
item.description: Pandora, the world’s largest jewellery brand, opened a production site in Ho Chi Minh City on Thursday, investing $150 million in a factory expected to create 7,000 jobs.

item.title: Belgian universities slip down higher education ranking
item.description: KU Leuven ranks 45th globally, obtaining its highest ranking since 2016.
